title: Natural forward affine Hom comparison, invertible in rank one
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open, A=Gamma(Y,U), and T the associated-sheaf functor transported by isoSpec [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. There exists a family c(M,N):T(Hom_A(M,N)) -> internalHom(T(M),T(N)) [def-pur-sheaf-hom] for every pair of A-modules, natural under precomposition by every map Mprime -> M and postcomposition by every map N -> Nprime. For every N, c(A,N) is an isomorphism. No invertibility is asserted for general M.

source.place: lemma-spec-sheaves, clauses (4)-(5) and functoriality; Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, finite free Hom coefficient map

proof.text: Choose the comparison uniquely specified by its values on global generators. Rewrite the explicit affine-chart functor to its named definition using affineHomComparisonFunctor_eq, without unfolding localization data.

For the chosen comparison, apply affineHomComparison_chart_left and affineHomComparison_chart_right to obtain the two naturality equations. These component theorems are proved from the generator normalization and the tilde adjunction.

Apply affineHomComparison_chart_rankone to the same chosen family. It gives rank-one invertibility by module evaluation at one and the internal-Hom unit isomorphism. Assemble the two equations and this isomorphism property as the three conjuncts.

based_on.place: Lemma 26.7.1 (lemma-compare-constructions), mapping property for arbitrary target sheaves; Tag 01HV (4)-(5), principal-open localization and restriction.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affine_hom_comparison_maps {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.affineOpens) :
    let A := (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
    let T := tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom
    ∃ c : ∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{u} A),
        T.obj (ModuleCat.of A (M ⟶ N)) ⟶
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
            (T.obj M) (T.obj N),
      (∀ (M M' N : ModuleCat.{u} A) (f : M' ⟶ M),
        c M N ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
          (T.map f) (𝟙 (T.obj N)) =
        T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.leftComp A N f)) ≫ c M' N) ∧
      (∀ (M N N' : ModuleCat.{u} A) (g : N ⟶ N'),
        c M N ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
          (𝟙 (T.obj M)) (T.map g) =
        T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.rightComp A M g)) ≫ c M N') ∧
      (∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A, IsIso (c (ModuleCat.of A A) N))
